# k0rdent_security_groups (Data Source)

Every security group in a project, including the platform-owned default group of each VPC.

A group with `owner_kind` set is the platform's. It cannot be modified or deleted, and attaching it anywhere but its own VPC is refused.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Only the groups you can manage, without each VPC's default group.
data "k0rdent_security_groups" "mine" {
  only_tenant_owned = true
}

# Active groups tagged team = "ml".
data "k0rdent_security_groups" "ml" {
  tags  = { team = "ml" }
  state = "active"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `display_name_regex` (String) Return only the groups whose `display_name` matches this regular expression, in the RE2 syntax Terraform's own `regex` function takes. The match isn't anchored, so `prod` finds `preprod-a`: write `^prod-` for a prefix. One with no `display_name` never matches. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Must be a regular expression in RE2 syntax.
- `only_tenant_owned` (Boolean) Return only the groups with no `owner_kind`, which are the ones a `k0rdent_security_group` can manage. Filtered in the provider: the list operation takes no filter for it.
- `project` (String) Project to read. Defaults to the provider's `project`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `region` (String) Region to read. Defaults to the provider's `region`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `state` (String) Return only the groups whose `state` is this value. Sent to the platform as the list operation's own filter, and checked again on what comes back. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["creating" "active" "updating" "deleting" "failed"].
- `tags` (Map of String) Return only the groups carrying every one of these tags with exactly this value. Tags beyond these don't matter. Filtered in the provider, after the whole list is read: the list operation takes no such filter. **Constraints:** Every tag value must be set: a null value matches nothing.

### Read-Only

- `ids` (List of String) Just the ids, for `for_each` and `contains`. Sorted by `id`, the same positions as `security_groups`.
- `security_groups` (Attributes List) The groups, sorted by `id`, which is the group's name and never changes. That order is stable under a reorder upstream but not under an insertion: a new group sorting ahead of one you read shifts every later index, so drive dependent resources with `for_each` rather than `security_groups[0]`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--security_groups))

<a id="nestedatt--security_groups"></a>
### Nested Schema for `security_groups`

Read-Only:

- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name, for display only.
- `id` (String) The group's name.
- `owner_kind` (String) `vpc` on a platform-owned default group, null on a tenant's own.
- `rule_count` (Number) Rules in the group, ingress plus egress.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this object.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state as last read from the platform.
- `tags` (Map of String) User-defined labels, as key-value pairs. Null when the object has none.
